Section 02

The wordmark

Two stacked elements: OHIO PRIDE in Montserrat, with OHIO in the foreground color and PRIDE in Light Blue, over a hairline divider centered on PAC. The hierarchy is deliberate: PRIDE (movement) sits above PAC (machinery).

On dark backgrounds (default for digital)

PrimaryWhite + Light Blue SVG PDF PNG
Mono WhiteSingle color on dark SVG PDF PNG

On light backgrounds

Primary DarkNavy + Light Blue SVG PDF PNG
Mono NavyPrint, fax, embroidery SVG PDF PNG

Square lockup

The same mark centered on a square field, for profile pictures, app tiles and anywhere a 1:1 crop is forced. Use the 1024 files for uploads; the full-size PNGs are 3127 square.

Primary on NavyDefault avatar PNG JPG PDF
Primary on WhiteLight avatar PNG JPG PDF

Banner lockup

For website headers, email banners, page covers and event collateral: the wide banner with the tagline and Progress Pride underline, built at 9:4.

Banner with tagline"Ohio's Statewide LGBTQ+ PAC" · 9:4 SVG PDF PNG JPG WebP

Clear space and minimum size

Keep clear space equal to the height of the "O" in OHIO on all sides. Minimum width is 140px on screen and 1.25 inches in print. Below that, switch to the OP favicon mark.

Endorsement badge

"Endorsed by Ohio Pride PAC" is a fixed lockup for candidates, campaigns and partners to display once Ohio Pride PAC has endorsed them on the record. Pick by background and never rebuild or recolor it.

White badgeDark backgrounds PNG JPG WebP
Blue + White badgeLight backgrounds PNG JPG WebP
Endorsement use only

The badge certifies a real endorsement. Don't hand it to candidates we haven't endorsed, and don't stretch, recolor or add a drop shadow. On busy photos, use the white variant with clear space around it.

Section 04

Color

Three brand colors, three roles. Navy is the foundation. Light Blue is the accent. White is the breath between them. Click any swatch to copy its hex.

Core brand

Progress Pride palette (accent only)

Signature gradient

--brand-pride-gradient · 135° · for thin dividers, the donate button fill and accent stripes.

--brand-pride-gradient-h · 90° · the animated sweep under the site nav.

:root {
  --brand-navy:         #152233;
  --brand-navy-footer:  #0D1726;
  --brand-light-blue:   #70D6EC;
  --brand-white:        #FFFFFF;
  --brand-pride-gradient: linear-gradient(135deg,
    #E40303 0%, #FFBC00 18%, #FFED00 34%, #008026 50%,
    #004DFF 66%, #750787 82%, #FFAFC8 100%);
  --brand-font-display: 'Montserrat', Arial, sans-serif;
  --brand-font-body:    'Roboto Slab', Georgia, serif;
}
Use deliberately

The rainbow is an accent, never default chrome. The raw Pride chips fail WCAG AA as text on Navy; for accent text on dark use --brand-text-accent, --brand-text-danger, --brand-text-success or --brand-text-warning. The full token file is at /css/brand-tokens.css.

Section 06

Voice and tone

Confident, not loud. Action-oriented. Complementary, not competitive. Nonpartisan, pro-equality. Institutional in feel, neighborhood in voice.

In one sentence

The clear, steady voice of an Ohioan who's done waiting: informed, organized, and ready to fight for neighbors at the ballot box.

Word choice

Use

  • Pro-equality candidates
  • LGBTQ+ Ohioans and their families
  • Ally / Pro-equality leader
  • Ohio Statehouse / Ohio General Assembly
  • "Build durable political power"

Avoid

  • Partisan labels in voice copy unless legally required
  • "Activist" framing. Use leader or organizer
  • Passive constructions
  • Naming peer advocacy orgs in comparison copy
  • Performative rainbow flourishes in headline copy

Section 07

Messaging pillars

Power behind candidates
Money and political muscle behind pro-equality candidates who act once in office.
Complement, don't duplicate
Advocacy orgs educate and lobby. Ohio Pride PAC builds on that work in a lane only a PAC can fill.
Nonpartisan, Ohio-focused
State-level, statehouse-first, anchored in Ohio's communities and Ohio's voters.
2026 urgency
Statewide offices, a special U.S. Senate election, statehouse races, and active anti-LGBTQ+ legislation make this a year that decides the next decade.

Section 08

Messaging rules

These are the lines we hold on every surface, from a Statehouse statement to a story sticker. If a sentence breaks one of these, it is not ready.

Say

  • Ohio's only statewide LGBTQ+ PAC
  • Out
  • Ohio Pride (general use)
  • Ohio Pride PAC (formal and legal contexts)
  • We (organization copy)
  • Pro-equality candidates
  • LGBTQ+ Ohioans and their families

Never

  • First statewide LGBTQ+ PAC. Equality Ohio built the ground we stand on.
  • Openly
  • Em dashes or en dashes. Use periods, commas, colons, semicolons.
  • Activist framing. Use leader or organizer.
  • Combative or base-only copy. We write for persuadable neighbors.
  • Naming peer advocacy orgs in comparison copy
Identity line

"Ohio Pride is Ohio's only statewide LGBTQ+ PAC."
Use it to close launch and resource posts. Do not add it to every caption.

Audience

We message to persuadable independents and purple-state voters, not only the base. Warm, neighbors not activists, receipts not rage. Build coalition; do not come in hot.

Section 09

Social playbook

Every graphic should still read as Ohio Pride with the wordmark covered. Two colors, one mark system, one idea per tile.

Formats

  • 1080 x 1350 portrait: feed default
  • 1080 x 1920: story and Reels cover
  • 1080 x 1080 square: only when a placement requires it
  • 1200 x 630: link share and Open Graph
  • 1600 x 900: X post

The two colors

  • Navy #152233 fields. Light Blue #70D6EC accents.
  • The Progress Pride gradient is an accent device only: divider bars, tags, thin stripes. Never the background field.
  • Accountability posts get their own treatment: near-black field (#0B0F14, --brand-accountability-field), white type, one warning accent. Never reuse it for endorsements or celebrations. The feed should sort itself at a glance.

The mark is a system

  • Wordmark in the same position, same scale, with clear space, on every template. Never rebuilt from type.
  • One brand mark per card: badge on announcement and hero cards, wordmark only on text cards, dual mark only on co-branded collabs.
  • Candidate campaign logos are used exactly as designed, never recolored or rebuilt. Give them a light field next to our mono navy wordmark rather than forcing them onto navy.

One idea per tile

  • One headline, one support line, one CTA max. Two ideas means a carousel.
  • Headline: Montserrat ExtraBold, 70 to 85 percent of canvas width, 3 lines max.
  • Support line: Roboto Slab, small. No middle type sizes. Scale contrast is the style.

Template families

News Response
Solid Navy field, big headline, Light Blue kicker.
Endorsement
Candidate name and race primary, tagline secondary, campaign logo as designed on a light field.
Stat Card
One giant number, one context line, source line small.
Quote Card
Photo, Navy overlay at 40 to 60 percent, quote, name and title, on-image credit for UGC.
Action Alert
Verb-first headline, one CTA, no fake tappable buttons.
Accountability
Villain palette. Descriptive only where the firewall applies.
Celebration and Awareness Day

People first

  • Real Ohioans over stock. Photos carry stories, flat color fields carry statements.
  • Alternate photo cards and flat cards so the 9-grid reads designed. Check the grid before posting.
  • Never obstruct a subject's face with type or other elements.
  • Scorecard and tracker content ships as designed graphics, never screenshots: one accent color, giant numbers, generous space.

Hard rules

  • No URLs on graphics.
  • No swipe cues or slide numbers on carousels.
  • No disclaimer on organic social graphics or captions.
  • The flat stacked-template look (navy field, stacked headline, kicker bar, support line, CTA, stripe footer) is retired. Cards should feel editorial and alive, fun or funny where the moment allows.
  • Rapid response target: approved graphic live within 60 minutes of news. Pre-build for Statehouse votes, committee hearings, court rulings, filing deadlines, election night, endorsement drops.

Accessibility floor

  • 4.5:1 contrast minimum.
  • Alt text on every post.
  • Captions on all video.
  • Body type readable at thumbnail size: roughly 40px or larger at 1080 wide.

Section 10

Captions

Every post ships with two captions unless a single voice is called for.

Versions

  1. Personal First person, the Director's voice. Personable, not cheesy. No invented first-person claims.
  2. PAC "We" voice, shared on Instagram and Facebook.

Structure (both versions)

  • Hook line (no commas)
  • Context
  • What it is
  • CTA
  • Link on its own line
  • Hashtags last

Rules

  • Emojis: 2 to 4 total. Never in the first three words. Never inside hashtags.
  • Hashtags: Proper Case, always leading with #OhioPride. 4 to 5 personal, 6 to 8 PAC.
  • No em dashes or en dashes.
  • Close PAC captions with the identity line on launches and resource drops only.
  • Firewall and judicial races: descriptive copy only. No express advocacy, no "vote for," no comparative endorsement language.

Example skeleton (PAC)

Early voting is open across Ohio.
Every endorsed candidate on our slate asked for this work and earned it.
This is the full 2026 slate, with a plan-your-vote link for every county.
Make your plan today.
ohiopride.org/vote
#OhioPride #VoteEarly #OhioVotes #LGBTQ #ProEquality #Ohio

Section 11

Compliance on creative

  • The standard disclaimer is "Paid for by Ohio Pride PAC." No personal names. Required on paid placements, mail, print, and signage.
  • Organic social graphics and captions carry no disclaimer.
  • Judicial candidates get descriptive copy only: no policy pledges, no opponent attacks.
  • Where a coordination firewall applies, copy is descriptive only. No express advocacy.
  • We take no public position on the 2026 governor's race.
  • Corporate and foundation money is never solicited for the PAC. Sponsorship and foundation asks route to Ohio Pride Action or event sponsorship.

Section 12

Digital specs

Favicon system

The favicon is the OP monogram over a Progress Pride underline on Navy Primary: a white O (Montserrat 600) and a Light Blue P (Montserrat 800), the same weight and color logic as the wordmark. Shipped as SVG, ICO, and PNG under /assets/favicon/, with a full-bleed Apple touch icon and a maskable 512 for the web manifest.

SVG
16
32
48
96
192
512
Apple 180

The web manifest at /site.webmanifest lists the 192, 512 and maskable 512 icons. Every page links the ICO, SVG, 32 and 16 PNGs, the Apple touch icon and the manifest in that order; the block is generated by npm run seo:build.

Link previews

The default share image is /assets/social/og-image.png at 1200 × 630: primary wordmark on Navy with the tagline and Progress Pride underline. Page metadata is generated from lib/seo.mjs; a page that needs its own card declares it there.

Theme color

Mobile browser chrome: <meta name="theme-color" content="#152233">.

Tokens, helpers and the consistency check

Every page consumes the canonical tokens at /css/brand-tokens.css and the shared header and footer injected by /js/site-template.js. npm run check:brand walks every public page and flags drift before a PR lands, and npm run brand:build regenerates every derived logo format on this page from the SVG sources. See docs/brand-system.md.

Section 13

What not to do

Don't

Recolor PRIDE to anything other than Light Blue, White or Navy.

Don't

Fill the wordmark with a rainbow gradient. The mark is monochrome by design.

Don't

Stretch, condense or rotate the lockup. Scale uniformly.

Don't

Place the navy-on-white wordmark on a busy photo. Use the mono white wordmark instead.

Don't

Use a retired mark. Only the files on this page are current.

Don't

Use the pre-v2.0 Pride orange. It was retired in favor of #FFBC00.

Don't

Add drop shadows, outlines, glows or bevels to any mark.

Don't

Give the endorsement badge to anyone we haven't endorsed on the record.

Section 14

For AI assistants and automation

Tools that generate Ohio Pride copy or graphics should read the machine-readable brand first and pull assets by URL instead of recreating them.

  • Tokens, asset URLs, and rules: /brand.json
  • Site summary for language models: /llms.txt
  • Canonical CSS tokens: /css/brand-tokens.css
  • Wordmark SVGs: /assets/logo/ (indexed by manifest.json)
  • Favicon pack: /assets/favicon/

Checklist for any generated post

  1. Navy field, Light Blue accent, Montserrat ExtraBold headline, Roboto Slab support.
  2. Official wordmark asset by URL, one mark per card, same position and scale.
  3. One idea per tile. Two ideas means a carousel.
  4. No URLs on the graphic. No disclaimer on organic social. No dashes in copy.
  5. "Only," never "first." "Out," never "openly."
  6. Alt text written. Contrast at 4.5:1 or better.
  7. Two captions: Personal and PAC. Hashtags lead with #OhioPride.
